title: Monorepo and Change-Aware CI

Verify the result using a controlled run or static check and interpret the evidence.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on monorepo and change-aware ci. content.why_it_matters: Monorepo and Change-Aware CI matters because it affects correctness, security, maintainability, or operating cost. Monorepo workflows can select affected components by path, but shared packages, lockfiles, and root configuration must trigger all dependent validations. A useful CI pipeline gives a clear pass/fail result for relevant quality checks. content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Monorepo workflows can select affected components by path, but shared packages, lockfiles, and root configuration must trigger all dependent validations. A useful CI pipeline gives a clear pass/fail result for relevant quality checks. Keep fast checks early, use services only when tests need them, and ensure required checks cannot be skipped accidentally. The most useful check is one that produces observable evidence and fails clearly when its stated requirement is not met.

items.title: Monorepo workflow design
items.text: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

items.title: Path-based filtering
items.text: For path-based filtering, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

items.title: Shared dependency detection
items.text: Declare job dependencies with `needs` and read prerequisite results or outputs through `needs.<job>`. Separate jobs do not share a runner workspace automatically.

items.title: Testing only affected components
items.text: Make the check deterministic and fail with a meaningful status when requirements are not met. Preserve reports where useful and configure required branch checks to match the checks the workflow actually emits.

items.title: Managing shared build outputs
items.text: Use an artifact for a file produced by a run, choose exact upload/download paths, set retention intentionally, and verify the downloaded file is from the intended run/job.

items.title: Ensuring change filters do not skip necessary validation
items.text: For ensuring change filters do not skip necessary validation, state the expected input and result, identify the relevant workflow field or operational decision, and verify it with a controlled check plus run logs. Document the failure condition rather than relying on the YAML file merely parsing.

content_blocks.code:
name: Web component checks
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "web/**"
      - "shared/**"
      - "package-lock.json"
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  web-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Run web tests"
content_blocks.expected_output: The workflow reacts to changes in web code and its listed shared dependencies; update filters when dependency relationships change.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Create synthetic changes to web code, shared code, and an unrelated directory; verify the intended workflow trigger behavior.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Do not omit lockfiles or shared packages that can change the component’s behavior.

content_blocks.title: Practice and verification
content_blocks.text: Inspect the example and make one focused change related to monorepo and change-aware ci. Predict the expected result first, then use the run instructions or a static review to check it. Record the difference between your prediction and the actual result. Do not add production secrets or grant write permissions just to make a sample pass.

items.title: Syntax and scope
items.text: Check YAML indentation and confirm whether the setting belongs at workflow, job, or step level.

items.title: Permissions and trust
items.text: Start with read-only access. If the example needs more access, explain the exact operation and reduce permissions again afterwards.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Use the run summary and first failing step. A green result is meaningful only when the intended checks actually ran.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain monorepo and change-aware ci, read the example, and identify a way to validate it. The wider system goal remains: Build CI checks that produce repeatable evidence and protect merge quality.

content.task: Apply monorepo and change-aware ci to a small workflow change. State the expected result first, validate the configuration, then record evidence from the run or static check.
task_acceptance_criteria: Identify the relevant event, workflow field, runner behavior, or security boundary.
Explain the expected success result and at least one failure or skip condition.
Use least privilege and a disposable/test context; do not include credentials or production resources.
hints: Start with the key behavior: Monorepo workflows can select affected components by path, but shared packages, lockfiles, and root configuration must trigger all dependent validations.
Inspect the exact event filters, permissions, expressions, inputs, and job dependencies that affect this example.
Compare the observed status and logs with the expected result; distinguish static validation from a real hosted run.
content.expected_output: The expected result is the behavior described here: Monorepo workflows can select affected components by path, but shared packages, lockfiles, and root configuration must trigger all dependent validations. The real result depends on the repository, selected ref, configured permissions, and runner availability.
troubleshooting: If a workflow never starts, verify the workflow is under `.github/workflows/`, the event and filters match, and repository/organization Actions policy allows it.
If a step fails, inspect the first failed step, exit code, stderr, installed tool versions, permissions, and runner/network state before retrying.
If a job is skipped or data is missing, inspect `if`, `needs`, outputs, artifact names/paths, and cache keys; jobs do not automatically share filesystems.
common_mistakes: Assuming YAML parsing proves the workflow runs correctly or matches the intended trigger.
Granting broad token permissions, printing environment values, or exposing a secret to untrusted code.
Using a placeholder command as evidence of a real build, test, deployment, or security scan.

A useful CI pipeline gives a clear pass/fail result for relevant quality checks. Keep fast checks early, use services only when tests need them, and ensure required checks cannot be skipped accidentally.
